variants.title: Size the service
variants.context: Capacity is the maximum work a system can handle per unit of time. Assume requests are evenly distributed and every server can sustain its stated rate.
variants.prompt: Traffic is 250 requests/second. Each server handles 100 requests/second. What is the minimum whole number of servers?
variants.explanation: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.50. Round up to 3: rounding down leaves requests without enough capacity.

mistakes.feedback: 2 servers provide only 200 requests/second, below the required 250.

variants.hint: Divide traffic by capacity per server, then round up.

variants.title: Plan for one failure
variants.context: Failure headroom is spare capacity that keeps the service working when a component fails. Assume the load balancer immediately redistributes traffic to surviving servers.
variants.prompt: You still need to handle 250 requests/second at 100 requests/second per server after ONE server fails. How many servers must be running before the failure?
variants.explanation: You need 3 surviving servers, plus one that may fail: 4 total.

mistakes.feedback: After a failure, only 2 remain. They can handle 200 requests/second, which is too little.

variants.hint: Calculate how many servers must survive, then add the one that may fail.

variants.title: Find the actual bottleneck
variants.context: A bottleneck is the component whose capacity limits the whole request path. Adding capacity elsewhere does not remove that constraint.
variants.prompt: Application servers can handle 250 requests/second, but the database can handle only 120 reads/second. Every request performs one database read. What happens if you double only the application servers?
options: Throughput is still limited to about 120 requests/second.
Every database read becomes twice as fast.
optionFeedback: Requests still wait on the same database. Application capacity is not the current limit.
The shared database remains the limiting component in this stated workload.
More application servers do not change how quickly the database can serve a read.
variants.explanation: The whole path is bounded by its slowest required component: about 120 requests/second here. Measure that component before scaling another one.
variants.hint: Each request still needs the same database read.
